messages.text: Hi everyone! *Applications are open for LawAI’s <https://law-ai.org/wrf-eu/|Winter Research Fellowship (EU Law)>*. The *10-week full-time fellowship* runs from 1 February to 9 April 2027. This is a high-impact opportunity for lawyers and legal researchers interested in deepening their understanding of AI and law and contributing to this field. Previous Seasonal Research Fellows have gone on to pursue legal and policy roles in the European AI Office, leading AI companies, academia, and think tanks, including the Institute for Law & AI (LawAI) itself. Fellows receive *a £1,000 weekly stipend,* a £7,000 relocation and housing payment, and work from our Cambridge, UK office, with *close support and mentorship from our staff*. Remote candidates will be considered in exceptional circumstances. We welcome applications from graduate law students, professionals, and academics with diverse skill sets, experience levels, and degrees of knowledge in AI law and policy. Applications close on *12 October 2026* and will be considered on a rolling basis as they are received. You can apply for the fellowship *<https://airtable.com/app5cvdeXoRE1FvKj/pag8dyaPFWfkFRMI9/form|here>*. We’re also offering a $1,000 reward to anyone who refers a candidate to us who we end up accepting into the programme. Read about the terms of the referral programme <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ETgnWJaw57YZZFTojUE5nRot5Ylo6e4hHNt3XrzBIcA/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.sv0x95v2xq5m|here>.

I'm interested in hiring swe contractors to build things for MATS but it's much easier to find people that can build things than to find people that can build things securely, especially if they need to be built to be robust to staff using our software with LLMs. Does anyone have recommendations on security engineers we could work with on pentesting our work?

Celeste Li and I are *launching <https://aistranslate.org/|Babel Translation>, which translates impactful English-language AI safety content into Mandarin Chinese for free! We’re (1) opening the call for translations and (2) hiring translation contractors.* :star2:

High-quality translations are very useful for global AI safety fieldbuilding; if you have impactful English-language AIS content, you should consider having it be translated. Our previous work includes the Chinese-language translation of METR’s OpenAI/Hugging Face Risk Report, & we’re assembling a team of strong translators with AI safety context.

• *To request a translation:* *<https://docs.google.com/document/d/1D5xk0az__sHpmAXvnFNsour9JPlAGso0nbed2KHyPxM/edit?tab=t.0|here’s a 1-pager>* with more info! DM me, email <mailto:hello@aistranslate.org|hello@aistranslate.org>, and/or set up a 15-min call <https://cal.com/team/babel-translation/lets-chat?layout=mobile|here>.
• *To join us as a translator:* we’re hiring paid contractors with native-level Chinese / Spanish / Japanese, strong writing and editing skills, and AI safety context. We’ll also support your general development in AI safety, through coaching and guidance. DM/email me, *and* please fill out <https://airtable.com/appD0QSGMLFDV7EYN/pag0SbynIYntVpqvp/form|this form>!

Unique AI Safety Op from Eric Huang at xAI.  Think carefully about this job as it will require a significant amount of swimming against the current.  You will also get a broad exposure to AI Safety work at a lab (as there are only 2 of you).  Remember what Buck and Neel have said about <https://blog.redwoodresearch.org/p/ten-people-on-the-inside|good AI Safety people on the inside>....

> The xAI safety team is hiring an fte to start immediately! I'm looking for strong engineers who will dig in and work tirelessly to make an impact. I'm currently the only person working on all production safety training and monitoring. To be frank, I'm completely out of capacity and need more help. Concretely, I expect a marginal hire to counterfactually allow us to run a smoother production training process and substantially reduce our short-term prosaic catastrophic risk. You will be given the lateral cover to take charge of the majority of safety production training, help fight other fires that arise, and implement whatever you think is the most important to get right across the stack.
> 
> This work will be challenging, but if this excites you, please reach out to John to express interest!
